name: Claymation / soft clay look
look: thumbprinted clay, imperfect forms, rim light, 12 fps wobble.

fits.notes: friendly consumer, kids, food, wellness, "human-made" counter to AI slop

when_not: Avoid for dense UI; claymation can't carry readable screens, so show the UI on a clay "device".

type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: chunky rounded display (Fredoka, Baloo, Recoleta); warm pastels, felt/clay colours, soft shadows.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour is the clay colour of the hero object; rest are warm pastels
brand_lock.type_role: chunky rounded display; the claim in the brand face on a clay device screen
brand_lock.world_changes: clay objects roll in and sculpt themselves; the UI is shown on a clay device prop
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: replacement-frame mouth/shape swaps, squash on 2s, fingerprint normal map, held-pose "pop" between poses
objects roll in as lumps and sculpt themselves
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects.role: soft photographic grain over the plates

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: claymation {subject}, thumbprinted clay, imperfect forms, soft rim light, smooth-clay look, flat plain green background, 3 variants per pose for boil
codex_assets.r1_note: clay characters/props on green screen, 3 variants per pose for boil; clay UI-device prop; texture tiles.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

palette: wooden/foley sounds, squishes, tiny glockenspiel, ukulele pluck

build.recipe: `library/motion/stop-motion/stop-motion-aardman-clay.md`, `systems/material/claymation-and-soft-clay.md`. Three.js: MeshPhysicalMaterial with sheen + noise bump + subsurface fake, rendered and stepped at 12 fps by quantising `t`; or 2D: Codex clay plates + A2 + A5 boil.

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: Plasticine studio
palettes.words: warm oatmeal paper, cocoa brown, tomato red clay, teal clay

palettes.name: Candy shelf
palettes.words: blush pink table, plum-black, orange clay, periwinkle clay

palettes.name: Garden clay
palettes.words: pale sage table, forest ink, mustard clay, terracotta clay

brand_lock.rule: Brand colour is the main character's clay; the table, props and ink are style-fixed. Use the brand hex only for the clay body, never for the lighting. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Rounded, chunky letterforms; or model words as clay letters in the plate.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

passes.role: fine plaster grain to hide CG smoothness

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: table-top 3/4 view, a shallow ground with a soft horizon; characters on thirds
composition.safe_area: 10% margin; clay figure at left or right third, big empty table for type
composition.fill: characters 40-55% of frame height, two to three props max
composition.product_ui: UI is shown on a clay-framed phone or tablet (thumbprinted bevel) and held by the character; never redrawn in clay

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: 50 mm macro-style lens at table height, shallow depth of field, slight low angle. Lighting: soft key from upper left through a diffuser, warm bounce fill, soft contact shadows. Material: hand-moulded plasticine with visible fingerprints, seam lines, small dents, satin matte. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: fingerprint impressions, tiny lint specks, slight surface wobble; no gloss. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no smooth CG plastic, no glossy highlights, no uncanny faces, no tiny readable text, no perfect symmetry.
codex.camera: 50 mm macro-style lens at table height, shallow depth of field, slight low angle
codex.lighting: soft key from upper left through a diffuser, warm bounce fill, soft contact shadows
codex.material: hand-moulded plasticine with visible fingerprints, seam lines, small dents, satin matte
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: fingerprint impressions, tiny lint specks, slight surface wobble; no gloss

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: hand-moulded plasticine with visible fingerprints; 50 mm macro-style lens at table height; warm oatmeal paper, cocoa brown, tomato red clay, teal clay.

sprite_sheet.rules: Not a sprite style. For a cut-out object or character use --transparent (flat #00FF00 key, then despill); one subject, no shadow plane.

do: Show thumbprints, seams and dents in every material
Hold the model in 2-3 clay colours plus table
dont: No glossy plastic or subsurface-scattering skin
No clay body bigger than 55% of frame
cheap_ways: Perfect Pixar-smooth plastic with a clay label
Neon colours that clay never has
